reviewer: Codex /root/mlx_integration independent source and AST/fake-file review
scope: Narrow pinned-snapshot policy only; not production transaction or execution acceptance
restart_policy: After accepted reservoir restore/startup, while provider is still stopped and held, atomically install a reviewed provider plist whose only semantic delta is the model argument. Preserve original bytes before any change. Bootstrap using the pinned plist so the choice survives a later launchd reload or login. Confirm replacement identity, readiness, packages, pinned model inputs and reservoir continuity before releasing the maintenance transaction.
findings: Exactly one argument changes: the sole --model value is replaced with the original manifest snapshot. Canonical launch plist keys, environment, working directory, logs, interpreter and remaining argv must remain identical.

The observed process uses the exact framework Python executable while the launch plist uses its venv alias. model_environment.command_matches accepts only that resolved interpreter family with an identical argument tail; this does not permit general executable substitution.
Existing local model paths bypass snapshot_download in the installed loader. The provider first reads that local config and still invokes its existing Gemma unified sanitize shim.

The current reviewed policy preserves original plist bytes for rollback provenance and requires a durable intent containing both rollback and applied pinned plist hashes before atomic replacement. The original mutable hub reference is not an automatic rollback target.

The prepared original manifest lists explicit defaults that are absent from the historical launch argv. Only its snapshot identity is substituted; this policy does not copy the manifest command wholesale into the production launch plist.

source_references.claim: Local config lookup before Hub fallback; same Gemma class override and sanitize shim.
Model argument passed unchanged to existing mlx_load.
Narrow framework runtime/launch alias family; command tail equality.

required_before_production_enablement: Revalidate the full original model manifest, package RECORD bytes, both interpreter executables and source closure immediately before any handoff; exact local snapshot must exist.

Finish and review fake transaction tests showing old drain identity is kept separate from pinned restart identity; original plist bytes and hash survive; applied restart hash is recorded before replacement; refusal/crash after each boundary leaves a reconstructible held state.
Review the minimal controller amendment for production scope and provider_restart_settings input binding. Current production-enable flag and controller admission both remain blocked.

Qualify durable retained-transaction reconstruction and an exact-phase recovery plan; in-memory anchors, guards and armed flags cannot substitute for recovery. Unknown override outcome must not automatically rearm, repeat a signal, or bootstrap.

Complete the actual frozen service matrix and separately execute the NEW restore_verifier using the installed original runtime against private preserved 192-node fixtures before production drain. A later stopped-production backup verification is a second check, not the first real execution.
Meet the existing quiet-host and memory gates before numerical qualification. No gate is waived by this policy review.
limitations: Current process loaded bytes cannot be attested retroactively from its argv or today's files. Preserve separately reviewed source/model lineage and label inference honestly.

Original plist is a preserved rollback asset, not an instruction to restore a mutable model reference blindly after any subsequent accepted pin. Rollback of the maintenance repair uses current accepted checkpoint identity and does not roll back runtime state.

Static path handling and fake argument tests do not qualify real persistence, production maintenance or MLX generation. Existing accepted fixture binds unchanged launchd primitives only; any controller changes require an explicit equivalence review or additional fixture.
These seven tests do not load a real checkpoint or verify native generation, TCC, persistence or production restart behavior.
Historical loaded model/source bytes cannot be inferred conclusively from the old argv or present disk hashes.
